articles.title: Couple with legs chained found dead in Tapi river, Dhule police suspect suicide
articles.summary: Dhule police find newlywed couple dead in Tapi river with legs chained; suicide suspected after man’s final call, investigation ongoing in Nardana.
articles.body: NASHIK: A 35-year-old man and his wife (19) with their legs chained were found dead on Thursday afternoon in Tapi river in Dhule.The deceased have been identified as Shyam Patil and his wife Sapna, residents of Padalse village in Amalner taluka of Jalgaon district. Nardana police suspect it to be a case of suicide after investigations.Some people informed police about two bodies floating in Tapi river around 12.30pm on Thursday. After reaching the spot, officers found that one of the legs of the man was chained and padlocked to a leg of the woman.Assistant inspector Sachin Kapadnis of Nardana police said residents of the area spotted a motorcycle parked near the spot since Wednesday afternoon. This suggested that the couple had drowned at least 24 hours earlier, he said.After identifying the couple using the vehicle’s registration details, police contacted the brother-in-law of the victim, Shyam. According to Kapadnis, the victim’s brother-in-law revealed that Shyam had called him around 1am on Wednesday and said “everything was over”.“Shyam told his brother-in-law that he was leaving, before switching off his phone. Shyam’s brother-in-law could not contact him thereafter despite making repeated calls,” Kapadnis said.Police suspect the couple drowned shortly after the phone call. Shyam, an employee of a private firm in Jalgaon, had married Sapna about four months ago. It was his second marriage. An investigation is under way to determine the circumstances that led the couple to take the extreme step.Key highlightsCouple found dead in Tapi river: A 35-year-old man, Shyam Patil, and his 19-year-old wife, Sapna, were found dead in the Tapi river in Dhule on Thursday afternoon.Legs chained and padlocked together: Police found one of Shyam’s legs chained and padlocked to one of Sapna’s legs when the bodies were discovered.Bodies spotted around 12.30pm: Local residents alerted police after noticing two bodies floating in the river on Thursday afternoon.Motorcycle parked since Wednesday: Residents had reportedly noticed a motorcycle near the spot since Wednesday afternoon, suggesting the couple may have drowned at least 24 hours before their bodies were found.Late-night phone call before disappearance: Shyam reportedly called his brother-in-law around 1am on Wednesday, saying “everything was over” and that he was leaving, before switching off his phone.Couple married four months ago: Shyam, an employee of a private firm in Jalgaon, had married Sapna around four months earlier. articles.title: Head of prominent gambling addiction nonprofit resigns after backlash to $2 million Kalshi donation
articles.summary: National Council on Problem Gambling executive director Heather Maurer required board members to sign NDAs before revealing the donation.
articles.body:
A decision by a gambling addiction nonprofit to accept a donation from Kalshi has sparked internal turmoil. In late September, the executive director of the National Council on Problem Gambling—the nation's largest nonprofit dedicated to combating gambling addiction—resigned after facing backlash over taking $2 million from the prediction market platform, according to a recent Barron's report .

Heather Maurer, who took the helm in January, finalized the Kalshi agreement without prior board approval and required directors to sign unprecedented nondisclosure agreements before revealing the donation at an April conference, according to the report. When directors pressed her on whether Kalshi had agreed to fund safety guardrails or promote addiction helplines, she acknowledged it had not, triggering months of internal revolt that ended with her departure less than 10 months into the job.

Maurer's resignation came just days after Jaime Costello, the NCPG's director of programs, resigned over differences with the organization's leadership.

"I made this decision because, over the past year, the environment shifted in ways I could no longer reconcile with how I believe this work should be done," Costello wrote in a LinkedIn post .

The upheaval comes as betting on prediction markets has become increasingly pervasive in the U.S. Prominent platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket let users as young as 18 trade contracts on virtually anything, though most activity centers on sports wagers. Both have grown rapidly, each reaching valuations above $20 billion. That growth has fueled disputes with states and Native American tribes over regulatory authority, while drawing scrutiny from sports leagues over game integrity and from advocates who say the platforms' accessibility increases the risk of addiction.

The NCPG has also faced fallout from state problem-gambling organizations and regulators. Washington's Evergreen Council on Problem Gambling ended its 35-year affiliation with the national group in September, concluding that the two organizations were "no longer sufficiently aligned." The Ohio Casino Control Commission also withdrew that month. The Nevada Council on Problem Gambling reportedly cut ties in August, as did the Michigan Gaming Control Board in July. All four said they disagreed with the NCPG's decision to accept a donation from Kalshi.

Donations from gambling platforms to nonprofits like the NCPG are not unusual. DraftKings had provided more than $2 million to state problem-gambling councils and NCPG affiliates since 2022, according to a March 2025 company announcement. FanDuel also donated $100,000 directly to the NCPG during Problem Gambling Awareness Month in March 2023.

But Kalshi's $2 million deal sparked backlash because the platform rejected the idea that its business was gambling. To accommodate that position, the NCPG created a separate "financial services and trading" donor category, setting Kalshi apart from sportsbooks like DraftKings and FanDuel, according to Barron's .

Clarification October 9, 2026: This article has been updated to clarify that state and federal regulators determine members' consumer-protection requirements.

This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Why is the Trump administration trying to dismantle the ICC?
articles.summary: The US has imposed sweeping new sanctions on the International Criminal Court.
articles.body:
Washington’s sanctions targeting the International Criminal Court (ICC) came hours after one of its former judges, Navi Pillay, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday.

The ICC was founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.

It has issued arrest warrants against more than 70 people, including Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu and Russia’s Vladimir Putin.

The US has denounced the court in the past, especially after it issued the arrest warrants for Israeli officials.

Washington has previously imposed sanctions on its prosecutors and judges, but the latest move seeks to cripple the operations of the court, according to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

articles.title: Mulher com tornozeleira escondia porções de crack em pote de tempero | G1
articles.standfirst: Ocorrência foi registrada na noite desta sexta-feira (9), no Conjunto Habitacional Macapaba. Os suspeitos já tinham passagens pela polícia pelo mesmo crime. A mulher usa tornozeleira eletrônica.
articles.summary: Tráfico de drogas em Macapá: dupla reincidente foi presa no Macapaba com entorpecentes e dinheiro durante ação policial na noite de sexta-feira.
articles.body:
Dupla foi levada para o Ciosp do Pacoval — Foto: Reprodução

Um homem e uma mulher foram presos por suspeita de tráfico de drogas na noite desta sexta-feira (9), no Conjunto Habitacional Macapaba, na Zona Norte de Macapá . Segundo a polícia, os dois já possuem antecedentes pelo mesmo crime. No apartamento da mulher, que usa tornozeleira eletrônica, os agentes encontraram drogas escondidas em um recipiente de tempero.

A prisão aconteceu após uma denúncia de venda de drogas em frente ao bloco 27. Segundo a polícia, a área já é conhecida pelo comércio de entorpecentes.

Um homem com as características informadas na denúncia foi abordado pelos policiais. Com ele, foram apreendidas 26 porções de drogas e R$ 83 em dinheiro.

Durante a ação, uma mulher que utilizava tornozeleira eletrônica e saía do bloco 27 percebeu a presença da polícia, jogou o celular no chão e correu para dentro do apartamento.

No imóvel, os policiais encontraram 64 porções de crack escondidas em um recipiente de tempero. Também foram apreendidos uma balança de precisão, materiais usados para embalar drogas e R$ 240 em dinheiro.

Os dois foram presos em flagrante e encaminhados ao Centro Integrado de Operações em Segurança Pública (Ciosp). A ocorrência foi atendida por equipes da Companhia Independente de Patrulhamento Tático com Apoio de Motocicletas (Patamo).

articles.title: Cabo Frio: Praia do Forte tem mar calmo e tempo firme antes o feriado | G1
articles.standfirst: A Semana do Saco Cheio atrai turistas especialmente de Minas Gerais e este ano garante movimento até o dia 18 de outubro.
articles.summary: A Semana do Saco Cheio atrai turistas especialmente de Minas Gerais e este ano garante movimento até o dia 18 de outubro.
articles.body:
O feriado prolongado começou com tempo firme e movimento intenso em Cabo Frio , na Região dos Lagos. Neste sábado (10), a cidade registrou sol entre poucas nuvens e mar calmo. Durante a manhã, os principais acessos apresentaram trânsito lento devido ao aumento no fluxo de veículos, mas a circulação já estava mais tranquila por volta das 14h.

Na Praia do Forte, um dos principais cartões-postais do município, turistas encontraram mar tranquilo e reforço nos serviços de limpeza, preparados para atender ao aumento de visitantes durante o período.

Tradicional entre os mineiros, a chamada Semana do Saco Cheio costuma impulsionar o turismo na região. Neste ano, parte dos turistas de Minas Gerais terá folga até o domingo (18), o que deve manter a movimentação turística aquecida ao longo de toda a semana, inclusive após o feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida.

No domingo (11), o tempo deve seguir predominantemente estável, com períodos de sol e possibilidade de aumento da nebulosidade ao longo do dia, com temperaturas máximas entre 26°C e 28°C. Na segunda-feira (12), feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida e Dia das Crianças, a tendência também é de períodos de sol e variação de nebulosidade, sem indicação, no cenário atual, de chuva significativa.

A partir da terça-feira (13), o cenário começa a mudar. Na quarta-feira (14), quinta-feira (15) e sexta-feira (16), a previsão meteorológica aponta aumento da instabilidade atmosférica, com possibilidade de pancadas de chuva e trovoadas. A previsão ainda é de médio prazo e deve ser acompanhada nas próximas atualizações.

No sábado (17) e no domingo (18), há tendência de melhora gradual, com retorno de períodos de sol. Também há sinalização de rajadas de vento mais expressivas em determinados momentos, especialmente no sábado (17).

Segundo a Prefeitura de Cabo Frio a administração aumentou em 50%, o efetivo de limpeza das praias, com equipes atuando pela manhã e no fim da tarde, além da instalação de dez contêineres híbridos, com capacidade para 1.200 litros cada, e 18 lixeiras de 240 litros, ampliando os pontos disponíveis para o descarte de resíduos na orla.

articles.title: Famílias deixam suas casas após deslizamento de terra no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa Civil descarta risco imediato de desmoronamento dos imóveis, mas moradores saíram por precaução. Avaliação com drone vai definir obras para conter erosão às margens do Rio Pardinho.
articles.summary: Defesa Civil descarta risco imediato de desmoronamento dos imóveis, mas moradores saíram por precaução. Avaliação vai definir obras para conter erosão às margens do Rio Pardinho.
articles.body:
Quatro famílias precisaram deixar suas casas em Santa Cruz do Sul , no Rio Grande do Sul, após um deslizamento de terra atingir a estrutura de proteção próxima ao Rio Pardinho.

O incidente ocorreu durante a madrugada e, segundo a Defesa Civil, foi provocado pelas chuvas contínuas das últimas semanas no estado . Ninguém ficou ferido.

Os moradores saíram dos imóveis por precaução, com o apoio da Defesa Civil . Os técnicos do órgão avaliaram que não existe risco imediato de desmoronamento das residências.

O vendedor Maiquel Roos relatou o susto que levou no momento em que a terra cedeu nos fundos do terreno.

"Eu estava olhando TV, estava na sala, quando de repente deu um barulhão no fundo do rio. Um estrondo muito alto. Pensei: deve ter caído do vizinho. A hora que fui para trás, eu só vi o clarão preto, então caiu todos os fundos da minha casa aqui", afirmou.

A situação gerou apreensão sobre os impactos de futuras cheias do rio na região afetada pelas rachaduras.

" Eu tenho medo . Quando o rio encher, eu sei que ele vai vir pra cá . Aqui vai ser um metro e meio de água com muita correnteza. Provavelmente vai ser muito, muito grande o estrago", disse ele.

O coordenador da Defesa Civil de Santa Cruz do Sul, Reginaldo Brito de Campos, explicou que o excesso de chuva comprometeu a estabilidade do terreno.

"Ocorre que, com um número maior de chuva contínua, o solo encharcado, infiltrando água, o sistema ali colapsou e aí ele desceu", disse.

Na próxima semana, a Defesa Civil deve definir quais obras serão necessárias para reparar os danos. A equipe técnica utiliza tecnologia para mapear a área afetada.

"Nós viemos novamente para fazer a avaliação com drone, para que a gente tenha uma visão de dentro do rio para cá, para a gente poder analisar perfeitamente e depois a sua engenharia propor quais vão ser as obras que a gente precisa fazer no local para conter essa erosão ali do terreno", concluiu o representante do órgão.

articles.title: Governanta relembra oportunidade dada por Virginia e Zé Felipe | G1
articles.standfirst: Nas redes sociais, Fran Chagas recordou a chegada a Goiânia após deixar o trabalho na roça. Ela agradeceu à família de Virginia pelo apoio e pela confiança no trabalho dela.
articles.summary: Nas redes sociais, Fran Chagas recordou a chegada a Goiânia após deixar o trabalho na roça. Ela agradeceu à família de Virginia pelo apoio e pela confiança no trabalho dela.
articles.body:
Fran Chagas compartilhou um agradecimento nas redes sociais ao relembrar a oportunidade de trabalho concedida pela influenciadora Virginia Fonseca e pelo cantor Zé Felipe. Na publicação, a funcionária definiu o casal como "anjos de luz" e ressaltou que a acolhida foi determinante para transformar sua história pessoal e profissional após se mudar para Goiânia .

A homenagem foi publicada na quinta-feira (8). A profissional relembrou a data em que começou a prestar serviços para Virginia, em 13 de novembro . Além de Virginia e Zé Felipe, Fran agradeceu à mãe da influenciadora, Margareth Serrão.

Ela ainda citou a confiança concedida e o que aprendeu durante a convivência, além das conquistas que alcançou. Em julho, Fran publicou um post realizando o sonho do primeiro apartamento e se declarou à influenciadora .

"Os dois anjos de luz que Deus colocou no meu destino, o Zé Felipe e a Virgínia, que [...] abriram a porta da sua casa pra me dar emprego e hoje eu conquistei tantas coisas que eu nunca imaginei. Sou tão grata a Deus por ter colocado essa família de bênçãos, do coração puro e humilde, na minha vida", disse Fran.

Governanta relembra oportunidade dada por Virginia e Zé Felipe quando trabalhou para o casal: 'Anjos de luz' — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram Fran Chagas

Na legenda, Fran relatou que veio da zona rural , onde trabalhava no corte de arroz , e relembrou as dificuldades enfrentadas ao lado dos sete irmãos desde o falecimento da mãe. Na foto, a governanta aparece sorridente entre Virginia e Zé Felipe, segurando um envelope e uma cesta de presentes.

Ela destacou que a decisão de deixar sua cidade de origem e buscar uma nova vida na capital goiana ocorreu em um mês de outubro, movida pela fé e pelo desejo de construir um futuro melhor. Nos comentários, os internautas parabenizaram o esforço de Fran. "Parabéns por mostrar sua história com orgulho. A gratidão é a maior virtude" , escreveu uma seguidora.

WOW!” he added.Trump has repeatedly claimed credit for resolving eight conflicts, including tensions involving India and Pakistan, Israel and Iran, and Israel and Hamas. However, India has consistently rejected his claims of mediation in the India-Pakistan ceasefire, maintaining that the understanding was reached after Pakistan's Director General of Military Operations contacted his Indian counterpart.The US President also criticised the Norwegian Nobel Committee for selecting Pillay, questioning her credentials and accusing her of being opposed to Israel. articles.title: In 1969, a Nevada man began turning roadside junk, bottles, hubcaps and car parts into a desert home; decades later, the five-acre Thunder Mountain Monument is a free roadside attraction
articles.summary: Just off Interstate 80 near Imlay, Nevada, a five-acre roadside attraction showcases an unusual collection of concrete structures and sculptures made from
articles.body: Just off Interstate 80 near Imlay, Nevada, a five-acre roadside attraction showcases an unusual collection of concrete structures and sculptures made from discarded bottles, car parts and scrap metal. What looks like a giant artwork made from discarded objects began as the personal project of Frank Van Zant, better known as Chief Rolling Mountain Thunder. According to Travel Nevada, Van Zant started building Thunder Mountain Monument in 1969, using materials such as old bottles, scrap metal and car parts to create a home and a tribute to Native American history. Over the following decades, the site grew into a five-acre collection of handmade structures that visitors can explore for free during daylight hours.How a roadside stop became a lifelong projectVan Zant's journey to Nevada was not originally a plan to build a desert monument. A World War II veteran, he had worked as a deputy sheriff and later for the US Forest Service, where he collected artefacts he found while preparing maps. In 1968, he travelled east from California with his wife. According to Travel Nevada's account, their truck broke down near Imlay, a small settlement between Lovelock and Winnemucca. The couple stayed in the area, and Van Zant eventually began building on the property.He adopted the name Rolling Mountain Thunder and developed a vision for a place that would honour Native American people and their history. He also spoke of spiritual experiences and believed he had a purpose in creating the monument. Rather than designing a conventional house, he started transforming a trailer and gradually expanded it with concrete, rocks and objects collected from the surrounding area. What began as a shelter grew into a much larger and more unusual undertaking.Building with what others threw awayThunder Mountain took shape through improvisation rather than formal architectural plans. Van Zant used whatever materials he could find, fitting discarded objects into walls, windows and decorative features. Old bottles became part of the walls, creating colourful patterns when sunlight passed through them. Car parts, hubcaps, windshields, railroad materials and scrap metal were incorporated into the structures. Concrete held many of these objects together, giving the buildings their distinctive appearance. Travel Nevada's account describes how Van Zant could turn an unwanted typewriter into a design feature or arrange bottles to form a makeshift stained-glass window. Objects that might otherwise have been thrown away became part of the monument's architecture. The result was not a carefully planned building in the conventional sense. Its unusual appearance reflected the materials available and Van Zant's changing ideas as construction continued.Over the years, he created more than 200 concrete sculptures, many depicting Native American figures and themes connected to their history and experiences. The site became both a personal residence and an expansive outdoor art environment.A home, a hostel and a spiritual refugeThunder Mountain was not always simply a roadside attraction. For years, Van Zant lived on the property with members of his family, and the compound also provided shelter for visitors. During the 1970s, the site attracted people travelling through the region, including members of the counterculture movement, some of whom stayed there temporarily.Van Zant's family life was closely connected to the property. He had eight children, and the main structure developed into a maze of rooms, stairways, unusual windows and walls incorporating car parts. His vision combined artistic expression, spiritual beliefs and a desire to commemorate Native American history. The monument's many objects were not merely decorations; they formed part of the personal meaning he attached to the place.However, the site also experienced setbacks. A fire in 1983 destroyed much of the compound, including a hostel. Van Zant continued living at Thunder Mountain until his death in 1989.Preserving the monument after his deathAfter Van Zant died, the property suffered from vandalism and deterioration. Its survival depended on people willing to maintain the structures and prevent the unusual collection from falling into ruin. The monument was recognised as a Nevada State Historic Site in 1992. His son, Dan Van Zant, subsequently helped preserve the property, contributing money and arranging repairs. The work has remained a challenge because the buildings were assembled from unconventional materials and were never constructed like ordinary homes. Today, a caretaker helps look after the grounds, while donations from visitors support ongoing maintenance. The site remains a reminder of one man's determination to turn an unconventional vision into a lasting landmark.Visiting Thunder Mountain Monument todayLocated near Imlay, Thunder Mountain Monument sits just off Interstate 80 at Exit 145. Visitors can follow the signs to reach the property and walk around the outdoor sculptures and structures during daylight hours. Admission is free, although donations are encouraged to help maintain the site. The main residence is not open for visitors to enter, and people are asked to respect fences and restricted areas.For travellers passing through Nevada, the monument offers something different from the state's better-known natural attractions. Its buildings and sculptures combine found objects, concrete and personal symbolism in a way that is difficult to mistake for anything else. More than five decades after construction began, Thunder Mountain remains a testament to Van Zant's resourcefulness and imagination. What started with a broken-down truck and a collection of discarded materials has become a distinctive roadside landmark, preserved for curious visitors who stop to see what one man built in the desert.You use AI every day. articles.title: One drone, three jobs: Lucknow Police turns to drone tech to aid flood-hit residents
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: In a first, Lucknow Police has turned to multi-functional drone technology to bring relief and security to flood-hit Faizullaganj, where
articles.body: LUCKNOW: In a first, Lucknow Police has turned to multi-functional drone technology to bring relief and security to flood-hit Faizullaganj, where submerged lanes have made conventional patrolling difficult and forced families to leave their homes.Equipped with a lighting system, live surveillance camera and public address system, the drone is performing three jobs at once — illuminating waterlogged streets, keeping watch over deserted homes and broadcasting messages to residents stranded by floodwater. It can also carry up to 10 kg of relief supplies to areas that are difficult to access on foot.Deployed in collaboration with Delhi-based robotics startup Aevon Dynamics, the Modular Aerial Policing Drone (MAPD) is designed to help police maintain a presence in inundated neighbourhoods after dark, when movement on the ground becomes challenging and evacuated homes may be vulnerable to theft.“UP Police is here to help you. Dial 112 in case of any emergency,” the drone announces as it flies over the flooded locality, taking the police’s voice to residents stranded on upper floors and rooftops.“The announcements are intended not only to provide emergency information but also to reassure residents who may otherwise feel isolated in the darkness,” said DCP North Amit K Anand.Yawar Sayeed, founder of Aevon Dynamics and an incubatee at Delhi Technological University, said the drone’s distinguishing feature was its ability to combine lighting, surveillance and communication in a single aircraft.“The idea is to have one drone with light, sight and voice working together. It illuminates the area, provides live surveillance to the police control room and makes announcements to people on the ground,” Sayeed said.According to the system’s concept note, the lighting module can illuminate around 400 square metres at a time, while the speaker system can cover approximately 2,500 square metres. Its onboard camera streams live footage to the police control room, allowing personnel to monitor rooftops, narrow lanes and waterlogged compounds that are difficult to access from the ground.From night patrols to relief dropsWith an advertised payload capacity of 10 kg and an all-up weight of 24 kg, the drone can also transport relief supplies to residents cut off by floodwater. Police personnel can then use boats to reach stranded families, deliver assistance and carry out rescue operations.DCP North, who is overseeing the police response in the affected area, said the deployment was part of a broader effort to maintain surveillance and assist residents in flood-hit pockets where movement remained restricted.Sayeed said Aevon Dynamics had been working with UP Police on drone technology for about a year. articles.title: In 2008, a California couple bought a home and found remnants of an old backyard railway; they rebuilt the garden train with a former Disney Imagineer, and the estate sold for $8.5 million
articles.summary: Some backyards have a swing set. But this one has a station, a tunnel, and a train that riders can climb aboard!
articles.body: Some backyards have a swing set. But this one has a station, a tunnel, and a train that riders can climb aboard! Tucked into the 1.55-acre estate in La Cañada Flintridge, a hillside community about 15 miles north of downtown Los Angeles, is one feature that not many homes can claim. In its backyard, there is a five-passenger garden railway that looks straight out of a fantasy film.When David and Sherry Kirchheimer bought the property in 2008, they discovered remnants of an old backyard railway. Instead of tearing them out, the couple decided to restore them and make the railway part of their home. The estate was sold for $8.5 million in 2025.The listing describes the property as ‘a captivating blend of stately, bucolic and magical’. That's a lot of adjectives, but the yard earns them. A 50-by-19-foot swimming pool with a diving board sits beside a two-level deck, a rose garden, and a pergola draped in wisteria. There's a fenced vegetable garden, citrus and oak trees, and a play structure with bridges and climbing walls. It’s more than what one would expect from a home.A railroadThe main attraction of the property is, of course, the Flintheim Railroad. It is a garden railway built for five passengers. The layout includes a train station with a crossing light, a tunnel, two bridges, a general store, and a mining camp. A replica of the Grizzly Flats Railroad shed also stands on the grounds. “This property has every feature you’d expect in a private estate, plus one not found elsewhere: a custom rideable train,” real estate agent Kathy Seuylemezian said.“The Flintheim Railroad is the modern incarnation of the area’s rich history of backyard trains, including a replica of the famous Grizzly Flats Railroad train shed.”Bill Tyson, a Walt Disney ‘Imagineer’, designed the backyard. “Evoking Disneyland, the railroad includes a train station with a crossing light, tunnel, two bridges, general store and mining camp,” a news release says.Inside the houseThe main house has six bedrooms and eight bathrooms. A grand foyer with a curved staircase leads to formal dining and living rooms. There is also a chef's kitchen with a Sub-Zero refrigerator and a wine fridge. A downstairs en suite gives guests a room without having to climb stairs.Upstairs, there is the primary suite, which has a sitting room, a fireplace, a balcony, and a bath with a jetted tub and double sinks. Other structures include a one-bedroom guest house, a gym above the garage, a workshop, and a game house with a pool table and a stone fireplace. According to the listing, the home has a 20-kilowatt generator, Ring cameras, and a San Marino security system for added security and convenience. The two-car garage and two-car carport are complemented by a large, flat circular driveway that can securely park a dozen vehicles. “The meticulously landscaped grounds, honoured with multiple 'La Cañada Beautiful' awards, are a standout feature,” the listing says.The estate was listed at $8.5 million. The mansion and its backyard quickly attracted buyers. The property’s proximity to the freeway and La Cañada schools also grabbed eyeballs.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Entire Delhi shut down; police, BJP's 'goondas' beat up students: Rahul Gandhi at Chhatron Ki Goonj
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP of silencing dissent, alleging that
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP of silencing dissent, alleging that the internet was shut down in Delhi and students were beaten up during protests in the national capital.“They are silencing voices as you saw in Delhi. The entire city was shutdown, internet was shutdown. Police was beating students. BJP released their own 'goodas' who were beating and thrashing students,” Rahul said while addressing students at the 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' event in Chennai.Slamming the Prime Minister over the alleged police action on student protesters Rahul said, "Modi is destroying India's democracy".The Congress leader's remarks came as protests rocked Delhi over demands for Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar's resignation and allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Protesters were prevented from reaching Jantar Mantar, the designated venue, amid heavy security deployment, with groups attempting to assemble at different locations across the city.Delhi Police had deployed around 25,000 personnel, including police and paramilitary forces, ahead of the demonstration. Restrictions were also imposed at several metro stations, while protesters were detained as they attempted to regroup and raise slogans.Rahul, meanwhile, linked the importance of dissent and questioning to the role of students in a democracy, arguing that curiosity was essential for progress and innovation.“We said that curiosity comes from your culture, your history, and your land. It is the basis with which you ask questions. Curiosity is also the foundation of your progress. Anything that you ever do, any business that has built, any country that has built, any innovation, any art, dance or music. Anything that you do well will always begin as a question that you ask. So, questioning is the foundation of curiosity, questioning is also the foundation of progress,” he said.He further said that curiosity gave students the ability to question authority, imagine the future and make choices. Rahul also argued that the Constitution protected citizens' right to question those in power, while voting provided them a means to seek answers. Opposition leaders slam Delhi crackdownOpposition leaders criticised the Delhi Police crackdown on protesters, accusing the BJP-led government of suppressing dissent and curbing democratic rights. Several leaders compared the restrictions to those imposed in Kashmir after the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019. 'If this isn't dictatorship, then what is?': Aaditya ThackerayShiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray accused the BJP of detaining citizens out of fear, questioning whether its actions amounted to dictatorship.“This isn't just about detention; the BJP is in a state of tension, which is why everyone is facing detention. It is the fear within the BJP that has led to the detention of Indian citizens. If this isn't dictatorship, then what is?” 'Why is it so afraid of the common man's protest?': Abhishek BanerjeeTMC MP Abhishek Banerjee alleged that around 2,500 people were detained across Delhi, including party workers, supporters and bystanders, and said even peaceful protests were being prevented.“This surpasses even the era of Hitler. If this government was elected by the people, why is it so afraid of the common man’s protest?” 'The Kashmir model has been exported to Delhi': Omar AbdullahJammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah compared the restrictions in Delhi to the situation in Kashmir after Article 370 was abrogated.“The Kashmir model has been exported to Delhi. Welcome to the New Delhi, modelled on the New Jammu and Kashmir,” he posted on X. 'This is how enforced silence is passed off as consent': Mehbooba MuftiPDP president Mehbooba Mufti accused the BJP of presenting restrictions on protests as public consent, drawing parallels with the lockdown in Kashmir in 2019.“This is how enforced silence is passed off as consent,” she said. 'It seems that the government is in danger': Kapil SibalSenior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal questioned the legality of detaining people travelling to Delhi to join the demonstration.“If a person or a community wants to protest peacefully, then who is in danger? The society is not in danger. It seems that the government is in danger,” he said. 'It does not want to listen to their concerns': Manoj JarangeMaratha quota activist Manoj Jarange accused the government of using force to suppress dissent and weaken the protest movement.“The protests were organised to raise issues affecting students and the poor. If the government is unwilling to allow people to protest for their problems, it shows that it does not want to listen to their concerns,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Man seriously injured in tiger attack at Yorkshire Wildlife Park
articles.summary: The attraction near Doncaster says emergency response procedures were "immediately activated".
articles.body:
A man has been seriously injured after being attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police have said.

South Yorkshire Police said it was called at 13:35 BST to reports of a man entering the tiger enclosure at the attraction near Doncaster.

In a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened".

The park will remain closed for the remainder of the weekend, it added.

The force has confirmed the tiger "attacked the man and this has resulted in serious injury".

Officers were attempting to contact his family, it said.

"The tiger remained in the enclosure following the incident and there is no wider risk to the public," the force added.

The park was evacuated following the incident and officers remain at the scene.

Police have urged people not to share "distressing footage" of the incident.

Karmelle Pelham, 39, from Worksop, was on a family day out when staff told them the park was being evacuated.

"We were in a lemur enclosure and somebody asked us to start leaving," she said. "Then, all of a sudden, we were being ushered further and further into the park."

Pelham said she had then heard what sounded like several gunshots.

"Then we saw a helicopter circling. That's when we started thinking, 'Oh, something's happened'."

She added: "There was big black tarpaulin over the tiger enclosure."

Pelham praised park staff for their handling of the incident.

"Nobody was really panicked," she said. "It was all very, very well organised. They did a great job of getting us out without panicking anyone."

Yorkshire Ambulance Service confirmed it had deployed an air ambulance, two land ambulances and a doctor.

The park said the safety and wellbeing of its visitors, staff and animals "remain our highest priority".

Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in April 2009 and its tiger enclosure opened in 2011.

Known as Land of the Tigers, it is described on the park website as an area where the big cats can roam woodlands and grasslands or play in a waterfall pool.

The park's other animals include lions, leopards, cheetahs, polar bears, brown bears and sea lions.

The BBC has contacted the park for further details.

articles.title: New York City has reopened Queens’ historic Lost Battalion Hall after a $25.9 million reconstruction, bringing back the recreation center with upgraded fitness spaces and accessibility
articles.summary: A recreation center that has served generations of Queens residents is welcoming people back after a $25.9 million overhaul.
articles.body: A recreation center that has served generations of Queens residents is welcoming people back after a $25.9 million overhaul. New York City reopened Lost Battalion Hall Recreation Center in Rego Park on October 9 following a top-to-bottom reconstruction. The project upgraded fitness areas, restrooms, entrances, safety systems and accessibility while preserving a building whose history stretches back to 1939. The reopening gives the neighborhood back an indoor recreation space with a long connection to New York's sporting and military history. A $25.9 million rebuild brings the center backThe reconstruction touched almost every part of Lost Battalion Hall. The weightlifting area, spin room and fitness room were refurbished and fitted with new equipment. Lockers and storage areas were upgraded, while the basketball court received a fresh coat of paint. The entrance and lobby were also redesigned, giving visitors a more modern way into the building while retaining its role as a community recreation center. The work was aimed at making the facility safer, easier to navigate and more comfortable throughout the year.Accessibility was a major part of the projectOne of the biggest changes is improved accessibility across the building. Lost Battalion Hall now has accessible restrooms on every floor and wider, safer routes through the facility. Doors were added at the front entrance, stairways near the entrance were relocated and enclosed, and existing staircases were rebuilt. A new staircase was also added on the east side. Restrooms on the first and second floors were redesigned with accessible stalls and fixtures. A former storage room was converted into additional accessible restrooms, while bathrooms that were too small for wheelchair access were turned into changing rooms. These changes are particularly significant for an older public building that was designed decades before modern accessibility standards.New safety and building systems addedMuch of the $25.9 million investment went beyond what visitors will immediately see. The center now has a new fire alarm and sprinkler system, a rooftop generator and a new water line. New water heaters were installed to improve energy efficiency, while an updated heating and cooling system will help keep the lobby comfortable throughout the year. Together, the changes modernize the infrastructure of a building that has been serving Queens for nearly nine decades.The Knicks once practised hereLost Battalion Hall has an unusual place in New York sports history. During the 1960s, the New York Knicks used the recreation center as an auxiliary practice facility. The building also became part of the basketball culture of Queens and helped nurture local players, including Queens native and former NBA player Kenny "The Jet" Smith.The hall is also home to one of the last surviving Works Progress Administration murals on New York City Parks property. The mural reflects the building's original connection to military veterans.Why it is called Lost Battalion HallThe building was constructed in 1939 after the Works Progress Administration allocated $100,000 for a two-story, 36,000-square-foot facility.It was originally built for the Queens Veterans of Foreign Wars and American Legion and included a firing range and drill hall. New York City placed the property under the jurisdiction of the Parks Department in December 1960, after which it was transformed into a public recreation center with a gymnasium and basketball courts.Its name honours the "Lost Battalion" of World War I. More than 500 soldiers from the US Army's 77th Division, many of them New Yorkers, were surrounded by German forces in France's Argonne Forest in October 1918. They held their position for nearly a week before reinforcements reached them.Now, 87 years after Lost Battalion Hall was built, the reconstruction gives the historic Queens building another chapter, keeping its original identity while updating it for residents who use the center for basketball, fitness and community activities.You use AI every day. articles.body: 38-year-old Venkatesh Sattaru, a US Army veteran, has been sentenced to prison on various charges of domestic assault in a spine-chilling case of suspected human trafficking that took place around 2022-2023. Sattaru, a resident of St Louis, brought his young cousin to the US and then used him as bonded labor. According to court records, Sattaru's cousin, an Indian, came to St Louis in December 2022. He was staying at one of Sattaru's houses and was asked to do all household chores and errands for the company that Sattaru owned. This went on for months until the cousin was shifted to a different house of Sattaru.Sattaru used to punish his cousin when he failed to perform his duties and confiscated his immigration paperwork. He did not let him sleep, physically abused him and restricted him his access to the bathroom, bathing and food. "Sometimes Sattaru punished the victim himself. At other times, Sravan Penumetcha and Nikhil Penmasta punished the victim, either at Sattaru's request or on their own initiative. The physical abuse included the use of dangerous weapons and resulted in serious bodily injury to the victim," the court document said.During some of this time, Sattaru, was also exaggerating his VA disability to increase his compensation under the Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers, also known as the Caregiver Support Program. The PCAFC provides monthly financial compensation to caregivers, who are typically relatives, to care for qualified veterans or service members. Sattaru fraudulently caused his caregiver to receive $83,776 in extra compensation from the Department of Veteran Affairs.All three individuals pleaded guilty. Sattaru pleaded guilty in April to one count of confiscating or concealing immigration paperwork while obtaining the labor or services of a person by means of serious harm or threats of serious harm and one count of theft of government funds.Penmatsa, 30, pleaded guilty on April 2 to one count of knowingly confiscating or concealing immigration paperwork. He is Sattaru’s brother-in-law. He was sentenced in August to 37 months in prison, consecutive to the 3-year sentence he received in St. Charles County Circuit Court.Penumetcha, 26, pleaded guilty on March 13 to the same charge and was sentenced in June to 30 months in prison.Sattaru was sentenced to 50 months in prison to run concurrently with a 5-year sentence for second-degree domestic assault in St Charles County Circuit Court. Sattaru has also paid a forfeiture money judgment of $74,634 to the Department of Homeland Security, restitution of $83,776 to the US Department of Veterans Affairs and restitution of an agreed upon sum to his victim.Who is Venkatesh Sattaru?When Sattaru was first accused of enslaving his Indian cousin in 2023, his former friend Karthik Bollam told FirstAlert4 that he met Sattaru in India, where he had strong political affiliations and got land in India. to the YSR Congress Party. Bollam said at that time that Sattaru was known for using his political powers to help people. He had a restaurant in India and when it started performing poorly, he reached out to people to come to the US.According to records, Satturu came to the US in 2008 and worked at a kiosk at a local mall. Then he enlisted in the Army around 2012, after he received his US citizenship. Court documents said he was honorably discharged in 2014 after suffering “lifelong debilitating injuries while in training.”After leaving the Army, Satturu started his own company Keysoft. articles.title: In 2025, California ran six 100%-recycled-asphalt road sections under a heavy-vehicle simulator; rain-triggered base shear failures and poor moisture control caused sections to fail
articles.summary: In a 2025 experiment, California tested six 100%-recycled asphalt road sections under heavy traffic conditions, revealing significant challenges linked to moisture control and base shear failures. This study underscores the complexities of recycling asphalt for road construction.
articles.body: Recycling an old road into a new one can cut waste, reduce the need for fresh aggregates and extend the life of asphalt materials. But a large-scale California experiment in 2025 produced a more complicated result. When pavement made with 100% reclaimed asphalt pavement was subjected to simulated heavy traffic, some sections failed sooner than expected, highlighting the importance of water, construction quality and the strength of the layers underneath.According to the University of California Pavement Research Centre, a Heavy Vehicle Simulator (HVS) was used to repeatedly load pavement sections with heavy wheels during the experiment. Six tests were carried out on a specially constructed track to examine cold recycled pavement made with 100% recycled asphalt pavement. The results did not show that the recycled asphalt itself caused the failures. Instead, investigators linked the most serious problems to localised shear failures in the aggregate base after heavy rainfall and to incorrect water contents in part of one recycled layer.Putting recycled asphalt under extreme trafficThe test track was designed to reproduce the stresses roads experience from repeated heavy vehicles. The pavement structure included a 225 mm aggregate subbase, a 180 mm aggregate base, a 120 mm cold recycled layer and a 60 mm rubberised hot-mix asphalt surface. The recycled layer used reclaimed asphalt pavement as its material and was produced using different recycling agents, including emulsified and foamed asphalt.The researchers tested the sections at two pavement temperatures, about 30°C and 50°C, and under two moisture conditions. Some sections were tested as compacted, while others were exposed to a constant flow of water. Traffic loading continued until a section reached either 12.5 mm of terminal rutting or a specified level of cracking. The results varied widely. The number of equivalent single-axle loads needed to reach terminal rutting ranged from about 200,000 to more than 15 million. The section that failed at the lowest traffic level was tested at high temperature and already had construction problems with foaming water and mixing moisture.Rain exposed a weakness below the recycled layerThe investigation provided one of the clearest lessons from the experiment. Heavy rainfall caused water to enter the pavement structure, and localised shear failures developed in the aggregate base. Once that underlying layer weakened, repeated heavy loading could cause substantial deformation even if the recycled asphalt layer itself was not the source of the problem.This matters because cold recycled asphalt mixtures can have relatively high void content and need protection from water. Earlier field and laboratory work has shown that pavement design, climate and the thickness of adjacent layers can strongly influence the performance of cold recycled pavements. A study published in the Journal of Cleaner Production has also found that climate and pavement structure are important factors in the performance of cold central-plant and cold in-place recycled pavements, while these recycling approaches have offered substantial reductions in energy use and greenhouse-gas emissions.Moisture control became just as important as recyclingAnother major problem emerged during production of the cold central-plant recycled material. Investigators found that the foaming-water and mixing-moisture contents used in part of one test lane were incorrect. Too much or too little water can affect how recycled material is mixed, compacted and performs under traffic.According to the California report, foamed-asphalt recycling depends on carefully controlled water content, as water is used to create the foam that helps distribute the asphalt binder through reclaimed pavement. The study found that the optimum foaming-water and mixing-moisture levels established during mix design had to be reproduced during construction. Departures from those levels in either direction could affect the performance of the recycled layer.The California experiment ultimately delivered a more useful message than a simple success-or-failure story. According to the researchers, properly designed and constructed cold recycled layers can perform well. But pavements with marginal aggregate bases that are vulnerable to shear failure when wet need extra attention, especially where heavy axle loads and extreme weather are expected.You use AI every day. articles.title: In the 1800s, US gardeners wanted beautiful purple wetland flowers, so they planted purple loosestrife; it later covered 500,000 acres and formed stands of up to 80,000 stalks an acre
articles.summary: Discover the story of purple loosestrife, a beautiful wetland flower introduced in the 1800s that became an invasive species, covering 500,000 acres and threatening native vegetation and wildlife across the U.S. and Canada.
articles.body: Purple loosestrife came to North America in the 1800s with European settlers, and some of the plant was brought in specifically for ornamental and medicinal purposes. The perennial wetland plant eventually spread through waterways and disturbed wetlands across the United States, with an estimate cited by government land managers that puts its range at about 500,000 acres across the northern United States and southern Canada.Purple loosestrife produces tall stems that are topped with dense spikes of purple flowers, and was used as a garden plant in various parts of North America. USDA Forest Service researchers say that it was introduced to the northeastern United States and Canada in the 1800s, probably through several routes, with seeds having arrived in ship ballast and animal wool, while the plant also intentionally being imported for ornamental and medicinal use. The U.S. Forest Service says that purple loosestrife was well established in coastal New England wetlands by the 1830s, and later introductions and natural spread carried it inland along canals, rivers and the Great Lakes. Its expansion accelerated during the 20th century, and became especially common in wetlands and other moist areas.The flowers came with an unusual growth patternPurple loosestrife can produce dense stands after they have been established, and USDA Forest Service material reports that infestations can reach densities of 80,000 stalks per acre. The plant can also reproduce in several ways, which gives established populations more than one route to expand. The National Park Service says a single stalk can produce as many as 300,000 seeds, while an established plant can have 30 or more stems and produce millions of seeds in a year, which are carried into new wetland areas through wind and water.The plant's ability to form dense stands became a problem for native wetland vegetation, and when purple loosestrife dominates an area, native plants can lose space and access to resources, which can affect the wildlife that depends on those plants. The U.S. Forest Service describes purple loosestrife as an invasive species and notes that dense, nearly single-species stands can dominate wetland plant communities. Its review also says ornamental cultivars have contributed to the plant's spread and recommends discouraging their planting in areas that are vulnerable to invasion.A garden plant became a wetland problemThe scale of the spread had become large enough for land managers to track it across regions by the late 20th century, and a Massachusetts watershed management document estimated that purple loosestrife covered about 500,000 acres in northern U.S. and southern Canada and was present in most wetlands used by breeding waterfowl along the Atlantic and Mississippi flyways. The figure was an estimate of the area that was affected by the plant across the region, and the USDA Forest Service separately records the species as occurring in all but six states of the continental United States in its 2002 review, with the Midwest and Northeast among its main concentrations.The same plant that had once been valued for its flowers was now being managed as an invasive species, and states began to restrict its sale and distribution, while researchers developed biological-control programs using insects from purple loosestrife's native range. The flowers remain distinctive, but the plant is no longer viewed just as an ornamental. Its dense growth can replace native vegetation and make control increasingly difficult in wetlands where it becomes established.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Hurricane Simon intensifies into category 4 storm near Mexico
articles.summary: Hurricane Simon intensified into a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico’s pacific coast on Saturday, raising fears of destructive winds, storm surges and
articles.body: Hurricane Simon intensified into a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico’s pacific coast on Saturday, raising fears of destructive winds, storm surges and potentially deadly flooding as it approached land.The US National hurricane center (NHC) said Simon was located about 115 miles (185 km) south-southwest of Manzanillo on Saturday morning, with maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (240 kph), as it moved northwards.The storm was forecast to approach Mexico’s west-central coast as a major hurricane late on Saturday or early Sunday. Further strengthening remained possible before landfall, the NHC said.A hurricane warning was in force along parts of Mexico’s Pacific coast south of the beach resort of Puerto Vallarta, including the area around Manzanillo, the country’s largest Pacific port. A tropical storm watch was also issued for areas farther south towards Lazaro Cardenas.The NHC urged residents in the warning zone, which includes the offshore Islas Marias archipelago, to complete preparations quickly to protect lives and property.“Simon has strengthened incredibly quickly, and that’s what makes storms like this so dangerous,” said AccuWeather meteorologist Dan Pydynowski.He warned that powerful winds could damage homes and businesses, while flooding and mudslides could destroy roads and hamper emergency crews’ access to affected communities. Power outages and damaged infrastructure could also complicate recovery efforts after the storm passes.Mexican authorities warned of heavy rainfall across the states of Guerrero, Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco.According to the NHC, Simon was expected to dump 10 to 20 inches (25 to 51 cm) of rain across parts of southwestern Mexico through Sunday. Isolated rainfall totals of up to 30 inches (76 cm) were possible in some areas of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, raising the risk of life-threatening floods and mudslides, particularly in mountainous regions.The hurricane was also expected to generate a storm surge along coastal areas near and east of its landfall location, accompanied by large, destructive waves, the NHC said.Swells generated by Simon were forecast to affect parts of Mexico’s southwestern and west-central coastline over the next few days, creating hazardous surf and rip currents, according to the Reuters.The NHC forecast that Simon would be near or just inland of Mexico’s west-central Pacific coast on Sunday.Last week, Hurricane Polo struck the Baja California Peninsula as a Category 2 storm, toppling trees and utility poles, flooding streets and causing other property damage.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Thanks for teaching youngsters’: Tharoor takes dig at PM Modi, shares 2015 tweet
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor late Saturday took a dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi by sharing his 2015 tweet about the Emergency.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor late Saturday took a dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi by sharing his 2015 tweet about the Emergency. Tharoor drew a parallel with the current situation in Delhi, where police cracked down on protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Thanks for teaching today’s youngsters many of the same lessons, Modiji!” Tharoor wrote on X while sharing Modi’s post dated June 25, 2015. In the old tweet, Modi had said, “Personally, the Emergency brings back many memories. As youngsters, we learnt a lot during the anti-Emergency movement.”Tharoor’s jibe came on a day of heightened security, mass detentions and a political showdown in the national capital, where a protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) was met with a heavy police deployment. 7,000 people were detained (and later released), including several Opposition leaders, while 45 Metro stations were closed till 10pm amid extensive security arrangements.Earlier in the day, Tharoor had criticised the government over the restrictions, describing the situation as a “war-like deployment” and saying that “our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ”.The Thiruvananthapuram MP said he had returned to Delhi after 2 am and had rarely witnessed anything like the security measures in place across the capital. He cited checkpoints, concrete barricades, spike strips, the deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary personnel, cancelled train services and reports of young people being detained.Questioning the suspension of internet services in the heart of the national capital and restrictions on access to Jantar Mantar, Tharoor said the government should answer questions about the integrity of elections rather than prevent citizens from raising them.“The government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression,” he said, adding that barricades would do nothing to restore public faith in the Election Commission.The CJP protest had triggered a wider political confrontation, with Opposition leaders accusing the government of suppressing democratic dissent, while the BJP accused protest organisers of attempting to destabilise the country.Delhi Police sources told ANI that all detainees had been released from detention centres except CJP leaders, for whom due legal process would be followed. articles.body: Hyderabad: Former minister and Andhra Pradesh MLC C Ramachandraiah has alleged that he was cheated of ₹25 lakh by a group of individuals who allegedly posed as owners of a prime parcel of land in Madhapur and offered to sell it to him. Jubilee Hills police have registered a case and launched an investigation.According to the complaint, the 77-year-old legislator, a resident of Road No. 71, Jubilee Hills, approached the police on Thursday night, alleging that P Tulasi Gopal, his son P Giridhar, and a few others induced him and his wife to buy a 5.5-acre property on the 100 Feet Road in Madhapur, claiming ownership of the land.“Believing the claims, I paid a token advance of Rs 25 lakh through RTGS. articles.title: Sec’bad roots to Mississauga’s mayoral race: Damerla adds B’wood twist to her campaign
articles.summary: Telugu-origin Dipika Damerla, ex-Ontario minister and Mississauga councillor, runs for mayor on Oct 26 with tax-freeze and governance pledges, plus Bollywood videos.
articles.body: Hyderabad: From a childhood spent visiting her grandparents in Secunderabad to a career in Canadian politics, Telugu-origin Dipika Damerla’s journey has taken her from Hyderabad’s cantonment area to the mayoral race in Mississauga, Ontario.A former provincial minister and an eight-year city councillor, she is now campaigning on better civic services, affordability and economic growth, using an unconventional mix of policy promises and Bollywood songs to reach voters.Damerla was born in Secunderabad to a family with an Army background. Her father’s postings meant the family moved frequently, but her grandparents’ home kept her connected to the city. She recalls visits to Monda Market and Secunderabad Club, and studied at Raja Jitendra Public School in Begumpet and Kendriya Vidyalaya in Trimulgherry. She moved to Canada in 1991 after her marriage.“We had Satyanarayan kathas and relatives visiting our house often. The Telugu films screened at Sheesh Mahal are an integral part of my memories. Those four years in Hyderabad were unforgettable,” she told STOI from Canada during a brief interview.Her campaign has recently drawn attention for its use of Bollywood songs. On Oct 9, following a mayoral debate, Damerla posted a video on X reworking the song ‘Kya Hua Tera Wada’. The clip ends with her slogan, “A city that works”, and an appeal for votes.In the interview, she said her team had been filming other campaign material when they decided to create something lighter. “It was just a gentle poke at myself. We never imagined it would get this much attention,” she said, adding that some of the response had been hateful. “The hate was upsetting, though,” she said.The lighter campaign material sits alongside a sharper pitch on governance. Having served as a Mississauga city councillor for eight years, Damerla said she believed the city could do much better, citing affordability, rising crime and the quality of civic services.“Why should residents have to put up with potholes in their neighbourhoods or litter in their parks? Govts have to act better and be accountable to the people they serve,” she said.Damerla has promised to freeze the city-controlled portion of residential property taxes for 2027. The freeze would not cover costs associated with road maintenance and waste collection being transferred from the regional govt to the city. She has also called for an independent Auditor General to scrutinise municipal spending and a review of the police funding formula.Beyond affordability and civic services, she wants Mississauga to become a centre for innovation, pointing to areas such as quantum computing and physical artificial intelligence.“I want to put Mississauga on the world map as a centre for innovation. These emerging fields offer opportunities to strengthen the local economy, and I want the city to be at the forefront of that growth,” she said.Her approach to governance, she said, has also been shaped by her experience of living in India. “When govts fail, people suffer. Failures in public education and other essential services have a direct impact on people’s lives. Govts everywhere need to respond better to residents and ensure public services work,” she said.Damerla moved into corporate banking after completing an MBA in finance from the University of Toronto’s Rotman School of Management and later ran a small business in Mississauga. After three unsuccessful attempts to enter provincial politics, she was elected to Ontario’s legislature in 2011, representing Mississauga East-Cooksville. She served as associate minister of health and long-term care and later as minister for seniors’ affairs before being elected to Mississauga City Council in 2018.Her links to Telangana extend beyond her childhood. In 2016, Damerla was part of Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne’s trade mission to India, which included Hyderabad and aimed to strengthen economic ties between Ontario and India. The wider mission explored cooperation in sustainable development, urban infrastructure, renewable energy and environmental technology. During the visit, Canadian company DataWind announced a partnership with the Telangana govt to establish a manufacturing base in Hyderabad.That year, Damerla was also the guest of honour at Telangana Night in the Greater Toronto Area, an event that brought together more than 800 members of the Telangana diaspora. She described the prospect of returning to her hometown and strengthening ties between India and Canada as “emotional and heartwarming”.“Trade between India and Canada could be so good. There is a fantastic opportunity to build on that relationship,” she said. articles.title: Gujarat HC upholds dismissal of judgewho slept in car on court campus
articles.summary: Gujarat High Court upholds dismissal of judge Asha Dave for sleeping in car on court campus, threatening protest and making offensive allegations against CJI.
articles.body: Ahmedabad: Gujarat High Court has upheld the sacking of a judge who was removed from her office for spending the night in her car on the court campus when she was not allotted an official residence at her new place of posting. The court noted that she escalated the matter by threatening to sleep on a footpath, attracting media attention, seeking the transfer of a sitting high court judge, and making offensive allegations against the chief justice. Dismissing her petition, the court said, “On perusal of the record, it is clear that the conduct of the petitioner was clearly unbecoming of a judicial officer.”The case involved Asha Dave, who was transferred from Vadodara to Deesa in Oct 2012 as an additional senior civil judge. Since judicial accommodation was not available at Deesa, she was told to arrange private accommodation. Instead of renting a house, she faxed the principal district judge at Palanpur seeking permission to sleep on the pavement, commute daily from Palanpur to Deesa and be allowed TA/DA, and have the collector requisition accommodation. She even spent a night in her car in the court complex, resulting in widespread media coverage.A report from the principal district judge led to her suspension and disciplinary proceedings in 2013. In 2014, she was issued two additional chargesheets over letters sent to the high court, including one requesting the chief justice and other judges to transfer a sitting high court judge, and another that the court described as “intemperate”.In 2023, HC’s full court accepted the recommendation for Dave’s dismissal. She challenged it before HC’s judicial side.After the hearing, the bench of Justice N S Sanjay Gowda and Justice J L Odedra said, “If a judicial officer decides to threaten the principal district judge and threatens to sleep on the pavement if a suitable accommodation was not provided, this conduct would basically be one which would be mocking the entire judiciary and showing the institution itself in a poor light. In our view, such a conduct, which is not in dispute, renders a judicial officer incapable of holding a judicial office and she cannot be permitted to continue in service.”Regarding her letter to the CJ to transfer a sitting HC judge, the court said that it is “on the face of it, obnoxious and despicable”.“A senior civil judge cannot by any stretch of imagination, address a letter to the chief justice and call upon the chief justice to make a recommendation for transferring a sitting judge of the high court,” the court said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ahmedabad | Silver Rate in Ahmedabad | Bank Holidays in Ahmedabad | Public Holidays in Ahmedabad | Ahmedabad AQI | Weather in Ahmedabad | Petrol Price in Ahmedabad | Diesel Price in Ahmedabad | CNG Price in Ahmedabad | LPG Price in AhmedabadStay updated with the latest Ahmedabad news. articles.title: 10,000-dhak drumroll, 1,000 shankha, 3,000 drones welcome Durga to her earthly abode
articles.summary: Kolkata’s Mahalaya at Eden Gardens and Red Road drew 40,000 visitors with 10,000 dhaks, 1,000 conch shells, 3,000 drones, dances and lasers.
articles.body: Kolkata: The Eden Gardens came alive to the beats of 10,000 dhaks, the sound of 1,000 conch shells and uludhwani as the curtains went up on the Durga Puja festivities at the Eden Gardens on Mahalaya.Dancers from different parts of the state presented their traditional dance forms, such as chhau and raibenshe, while singers enthralled the 40,000-strong crowd, which converged on the stadium to mark the onset of Matri Paksha, with agamani songs and Rabindrasangeet. The sky lit up with a spectacular drone and laser show as well as fireworks, illuminating the horizon. The sky show was put up using 3,000 drones. The gallery at Eden Gardens was packed as more than 40,000 people joining the cultural show to welcome Durga to her earthly abode. Visitors started queuing up in front of Eden Gardens from 4 pm, about one-and-a-half hours before the beginning of the show. Around 40,000 traditional hand fans were distributed.The event was inaugurated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, governor R N Ravi and other ministers and dignitaries. As soon as the CM reached the venue, the sounds of conch shells, uludhwani and dhaks reverberated around the stadium, marking the start of the four-hour-long show. Fireworks went off, lighting up a slice of the night sky above the ‘Paradise for Cricket Fans’.Sayam Bhadra, grandson of Birendrakishore Bhadra, the legendary voice behind Mahisasuramardini, was felicitated by chief minister Adhikari.Samarjit Roy, a Hazra resident and a cricket enthusiast, said, “I have been visiting Eden Gardens since childhood to watch cricket matches but this is the first time that I attended a cultural programme at this stadium. This is a new experience in my life altogether.”Among the spectators were many who visited from adjacent districts to be part of the colourful event. Rakhi Patra from Midnapore said, “We have come to Kolkata only to watch this Mahalaya event. We reached Esplanade around 3 pm. We will return home once the programme ends.”Heavy police deployment created a ring around Eden Gardens and Red Road. Apart from managing the traffic, cops remained on their toes streamlining the crowd, and directing the visitors to their different gates for entry into the stadium. Those who had not managed a ticket earlier were seen gathered outside the Eden Gardens gates, hoping to get entry passes, so that they could catch a glimpse of what was happening inside. Police said these visitors, without entry passes, came directly from Red Road, where another cultural show was organised.On the two sides of Red Road, separate daises for the different districts of Bengal were built. Dance and folk performances unique to the districts were performed, such as ‘ghora naach’ from East Burdwan, Astak from North 24 Parganas, Bonbibi Pala from South 24 Parganas. The entire road was decked up with various objects, all colour-themed in bright red and cream. Small ‘Durga Puja festival’ flags were handed out to visitors.Jagannath Chaiyal, a folk artiste from Bongaon, who was at Red Road on request from the state govt, said he had participated in the post-puja carnival on Red Road till last year. “The two programmes are of different kinds. In the post-puja carnival, idols being taken through the road to be immersed in the Hooghly. Here, we are witnessing dance forms of various districts. This year’s event is more colourful,” he said.In this first pre-Durga Puja event on Red Road, the southbound flank was kept open to visitors, while the northbound flank was sealed off for the chief minister, ministers and dignitaries.Adhikari first arrived at the PWD tent, from where he went to Red Road. He chose to walk down Red Road, waving at the crowd on the two sides and at performers on the daises, built along the way. Indian cricketer Richa Ghosh, actors Rituparna Sengupta, Ankush Hazra and Oindrila Sen and cabinet ministers, including Sharadwat Mukherjee, Purnima Chakraborty, Agnimitra Paul and Umesh Rai, accompanied him.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: San Diego under rare tropical storm watch with Rachel set to bring coastal flooding, heavy rain and strong winds
articles.summary: San Diego is under a tropical storm watch for only the second time on record as Tropical Storm Rachel is forecast to make landfall in Mexico’s northern Baja California Peninsula early Sunday morning, bringing coastal flooding, high winds and inland flash flooding from Southern California to the Desert Southwest.
articles.body: San Diego is under a tropical storm watch for only the second time on record as Tropical Storm Rachel is forecast to make landfall in Mexico’s northern Baja California Peninsula early Sunday morning, bringing coastal flooding, high winds and inland flash flooding from Southern California to the Desert Southwest. A Level 3 of 4 threat of flooding rainfall has been issued for Saturday night through Sunday from parts of Southern California to southern Nevada, southwest Utah and northwest Arizona, including San Diego and Las Vegas. This means numerous flash flood events are expected, with significant impacts possible. San Diego and Las Vegas could see an inch or more of rainfall from this storm. That is about double the rainfall they usually see in all of October in San Diego, and triple that in Las Vegas. This raises the likelihood for flash flooding in desert areas, which cannot rapidly absorb intense bursts of rainfall. Peak wind gusts in and around San Diego are expected early Sunday morning, and will most likely range from 25 to 40 mph in lower elevations to 50 to 70 mph in the mountains. Stronger gusts are possible if Rachel takes a more northerly track or they could trend weaker if Rachel shifts farther south, according to the National Weather Service. The only other time that San Diego was under a tropical storm watch was for Hurricane Hilary in 2023, the first year that such forecast alerts began to be issued for this region. There were infrequent and tropical weather systems that affected Southern California before 2023, according to the NWS forecast office in San Diego, but they did not trigger such watches or warnings. Wind gusts between 45 to 55 mph are expected inland across the Desert Southwest in parts of Arizona, southern Nevada and Utah on Sunday. Coastal flooding is a significant concern with Rachel, particularly in areas that have already been damaged by high waves and unusually high tides in recent months. Southern California’s coastline is expected to see coastal flooding as Rachel’s waves move toward the coast on top of pre-existing high-water levels. This could flood roads and damage structures along the coast, especially around times of high tide both Saturday and Sunday. The morning high tide is between 9 to 10 a.m. PT and the evening one peaks around 10 p.m. PT. A coastal flood warning is in effect from the Malibu coast and Los Angeles County beaches to coastal San Diego County until Sunday afternoon. According to the National Hurricane Center, “life-threatening surf and rip current conditions” are likely along the coasts of Southern California and northern Baja California. Coastal water levels have already been running unusually high in California due in part to the near-record strong super El Niño event in the tropical Pacific, which results in higher-than-average water levels and coastal flooding along the West Coast. In some areas, homes have already been lost to the sea. Waves from powerful offshore hurricanes in the eastern Pacific have worsened the coastal flooding situation in Southern California in particular. “Major coastal flooding has already been occurring in some areas, with observed water levels running as much as 1.5 feet above predictions,” the Hurricane Center stated. The NHC warned that hazardous coastal conditions are expected to continue next week, even as Tropical Storm Rachel dissipates over the southwestern states.
